**(0451707) Thematic Exegesis** (3 Cr. H.)  
This course discusses definition, history advantages, types, development, and sources of this kind of exegesis. The unity of each chapter in the Qur'an and how to reveal it. It also will include applied study on chosen subjects and chapters of the Qur'an.

**(0431709) Qur'anic Verses Related to Legislation** (3 Cr. H.)  
This course deals with the legislative verses of the Qur'an as referred to/in Islamic resources both the original and the contemporary ones. The course also deals with the importance of this type of knowledge and methodologies of deducing the rulings from the Qur'an and the difference between exegesis of jurisprudence and legislative verses. Also, the course deals with exegete's opinions and their methodology in directing and explaining this sort of verses.

**(0431710) The Qur'anic Recitations** (3 Cr. H.)  
This course defines the various readings of the Qur'an, the conditions to accept a reading, its types, and if the sound chain of transmission is enough to accept the reading or if tawatur is a condition also, their relation to the various modes (7 ahruf) the origins of the seven reading and the ten readings and the way of its transmission. The course also introduces biographies of the famous scholars of recitation of the Qur'an (al-qurra'), the foundations and methodology of each reading as well as the foundation of the Tasbee', T'sheer and Ifrad. Finally, it deals with the interrelation with the exegesis, Tajweed, Qur'anic spelling and the verses counting.

**(0431716) Language and Rhetoric in the Qur'an** (3 Cr. H.)  
This course explains the importance of Arabic grammar in interpreting the Qur'an as it was revealed in Arabic and according to their style of speech. The course shows the implications of the various grammatical situations and the alternation in prepositions and how they impact the meanings of the Qur'an. The course also deals with Qur'anic rhetoric and its definition and its importance in revealing the inimitability of the Qur'an, the synonymousness in the Qur'an, the distinguishing features of the Qur'an and other related topics such as metaphor, metonymy and other rhetorical aspects of the Qur'an.

**(0401717) Modern Trends of Exegesis** (3 Cr. H.)  
This course clarifies the most important methodologies of modern Exegesis including: rational, scientific, social, mystic, shii', and salafi and salaf in a comparative way and explains its concept, regulations, advantages and disadvantages and the impact of the interaction with other cultures on each of these trends in a critical method.
